title: The Image of the Invisible God
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Slow down and stare at this: the invisible God has been made visible. In Jesus, what was unknowable has been made known.
exhortation: So often we skim right past scriptures without seeing the wonders they hold. It's like driving past the Grand Canyon without looking up from your phone, or worse, glancing at it and shrugging. So let's slow down and just stare for a moment at what we've read: "He is the image of the invisible God."
An image is something you see. It's displayed, visible, physical, something you can behold with your eyes. Jesus is the visible image of the invisible God. That is mind-bending.

We live in a time when sight is what we have, but faith is what we need. If we stop and think about how complex the universe is, from the spinning of electrons inside an atom to the movement of billions of stars and the orbits of the planets, the evidence of an unseen God abounds. Even our own consciousness, the fact that you can think and ponder your own existence, is a flashing sign that there is more to this world than what we can see and touch.

And the miraculous truth of Colossians is this: where do we see that unseen reality, the one we know deep in our gut is real? We see it in the person of Jesus Christ. In Christ, what was invisible and unknowable has been made known. Lord, thank you for making yourself known to us, and for your word, which displays your glory for us to see. Help us stop, ponder and look on the glory you have revealed.
prayer: We worship you, Lord. You are transcendent and high above all things. Through most of your word, the thought of looking on the invisible God would have brought terror. But in Jesus you have made yourself known.

May we not run past it with casual indifference. May we gaze on you in wonder today, and may it spark joy in our hearts, so that we overflow with joy at all the glories and riches we find in you, Jesus. Thank you, Lord. Amen.
